newsitem.title: USA: PG&E to buy Bechtel's stake in USGen venture.
newsitem.headline: PG&E to buy Bechtel's stake in USGen venture.

text.p: PG&E Corp and Bechtel Enterprises Inc said Thursday PG&E will buyout Bechtel's interest in their joint venture, U.S. Generating Co and its power marketing affiliate USGen Power Services LP.
Terms were not disclosed. The companies said the sale is contingent on third party approvals and is expected to close by year end.

"USGen, with its demonstrated success as a competitive electricity generator, is a key element in attaining our business objectives," PG&E president and chief executive officer Robert Glynn Jr. said in a press release. "This transaction will enhance PG&E's position in the competitive electric generation sector as deregulation of the nation's electric power supply industry moves forward."
USGen is a Bethesda, Md.-based joint venture formed by PG&E and Bechtel in 1989 to develop, own and manage independent power production facilities in North America, the companies said.

USGen, with regional offices in Boston, San Francisco and Atlanta, has ownership or management interests in 17 electric generating facilities operating in eight states, representing a $5 billion capital investment and nearly 3,400 megawatts of generating capacity, the companies said.
USGen and USGen Power Services sold 21.4 million megawatt-hours of electricity into the wholesale market in 1996, they said.
Bechtel will continue to provide engineering, construction and related services to PG&E, Bechtel president and chief executive officer John Carter said.

USGen preisdent and chief executive officer Joseph Kearney will continue in that capacity following the purchase, the companies said. Kearney will also become a senior vice president of PG&E upon the close of the transaction.
